description: The verifier-engagement task. Session 1 asks the agent to save 5 findings as PROSE with backticked symbol names + file:line — exactly the shape projmem's auto-extract recognises (`X` is defined at file:line). For arm C, every `note add` body produces a structured FACT claim for free, no `--claims` syntax required. Drift deletes 2 of the 5 cited files. Session 2 asks 'Of your 5 saved findings, which are STILL TRUE in the current code?' Projmem agent has `contradicted_count > 0` waiting in `projmem notes` — answer is one tool-call. Scratchpad agent has 5 sentences in notes.md that each need manual re-verification — answer requires N file-reads. Hypothesis: equal correctness (both can answer if they investigate); projmem uses fewer tokens because the answer is pre-computed.

sessions.name: session_1_save_findings
sessions.prompt:
You are starting a multi-session task on this ysoserial Java repository. TASK FOR SESSION 1: confirm the location of these FIVE payload classes by inspecting the source, then SAVE each finding to your persistence layer.

Findings to confirm and save:
  - F1: AspectJWeaver — find the .java file that defines `class AspectJWeaver`
  - F2: BeanShell1 — find the .java file that defines `class BeanShell1`
  - F3: Spring2 — find the .java file that defines `class Spring2`
  - F4: URLDNS — find the .java file that defines `class URLDNS`
  - F5: Vaadin1 — find the .java file that defines `class Vaadin1`

When saving each finding, write the body as ONE SENTENCE in this exact form (the backticks matter, the `file:line` format matters):

  `<ClassName>` is defined at <file>:<line>

Example: ``AspectJWeaver` is defined at src/main/java/ysoserial/payloads/AspectJWeaver.java:32`

For projmem use `projmem note add <target> --kind note '<body>'` (one note per finding); for scratchpad append each sentence to `notes.md`; for baseline you have nothing to save to. Output the 5 sentences to stdout as well so a human can audit. Be efficient: under 90 seconds total.

sessions.name: session_2_what_still_true
sessions.prompt:
You are continuing the prior session's task on the ysoserial repository. The codebase has CHANGED since your prior visit. TASK FOR SESSION 2: of the FIVE findings F1-F5 you saved in session 1, tell me which are STILL TRUE in the current code and which are now BROKEN.

Output STRICTLY this format:

F1: <STILL_TRUE|BROKEN|NO_RECORD>
F2: <STILL_TRUE|BROKEN|NO_RECORD>
F3: <STILL_TRUE|BROKEN|NO_RECORD>
F4: <STILL_TRUE|BROKEN|NO_RECORD>
F5: <STILL_TRUE|BROKEN|NO_RECORD>

Rules:
  - STILL_TRUE — the file you cited still defines the class at the cited line.
  - BROKEN — the file is gone, OR the class is no longer defined there.
  - NO_RECORD — you have no record of session 1's findings.

Use your tools efficiently. Projmem users: `projmem notes` shows the truth-status of saved FACT claims directly (`contradicted_count > 0` means at least one is BROKEN; per-note `staleness: contradicted` names them). Scratchpad users: re-verify each by reading the file. Baseline users: you likely have no record.
